- When sentiment is negative (e.g., -0.25 or below), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% to counteract sentiment-driven pessimism.
- After a recent spike in price (e.g., >70), model often overshoots in the next 5–7 days; cap forecast peak at +3–5% above prior high to avoid overbought bias.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (0.00–0.50), model underestimates upward momentum; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for the next 3–5 days to capture mean reversion bias.
- Model consistently underpredicts late-period (last 10–15 days) price increases; apply a 1–2% upward bias to final 5–7 days of forecast horizon.
- When sentiment is flat or negative, model exhibits lagged response; delay peak forecast by 1–2 days and reduce early forecast volatility to match sentiment inertia.
